item.title: The Age of Gated Recessions
item.description: Aggregate economic indicators are obscuring a widening divide between those enjoying rapid income growth and those facing deteriorating job prospects. The rise of AI could deepen this disparity, with certain regions and workers experiencing recession-like conditions while others enjoy boom times.

item.title: The AI Curse
item.description: Every sanction that ordinary citizens have ever possessed—the ability to withhold labor, taxes, sons, or votes—presupposes someone who needs what you can withhold. As AI infrastructure encroaches on Americans, they are learning the lesson of many resource-rich states: where there is no need, there is no democracy.

item.title: Where Will the Global Bond Rout Hit Growth and Equities?
item.description: In the US, the recent rise in bond yields is largely driven by structural factors like the end of the post-2008 Great Stagnation, higher potential growth from tech-industry investments, and greater private-sector demand for credit. Higher yields are more worrisome for advanced economies that are stagnating and innovating less.

item.title: Trump’s Korean Catastrophe
item.description: Donald Trump seems not to appreciate that deterrence depends on the ability to mount a credible defense. This makes the Korean Peninsula a more dangerous place, not least because 28,000 US troops are stationed in South Korea, which the US is obliged by treaty to defend.

item.title: The Dollar’s Outer Defenses Have Been Breached
item.description: The puzzle of why the Trump administration is so concerned with a falling yen has historical parallels not to the 1930s or the 1980s, but to the 1960s, when US officials feared that a crisis elsewhere could spread to America. With US bond yields spiking, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent is getting desperate.

item.title: Why the World Still Needs Wall Street
item.description: Outside of the United States, all other financial systems face major constraints on their ability to absorb large financial inflows. That is why geopolitical multipolarity is advancing faster than financial multipolarity, despite the many reasons that investors have to pursue greater diversification.

item.title: Aging Populations Need Not Mean Frailer Economies
item.description: Governments and economists have long viewed demographic aging as a threat to economic growth. But new research finds that labor scarcity encourages investment and shifts innovation toward labor-saving technologies, boosting productivity enough to offset a shrinking workforce.

item.title: Who’s Afraid of Chinese Surpluses?
item.description: China recorded the largest trade surplus in history last year, and its exports continue to grow. But the scale of the threat to the global economy, and the appropriate response, remains subject to considerable disagreement. Some economists advocate protectionist measures, if only to pressure China to commit to economic rebalancing, others argue that tariffs won’t help, and still others think the specter of another “China shock” is a bogeyman, because China’s surpluses do more good than harm.

item.title: The Big Picture
Only Protectionism Can Safeguard European Industry
item.description: While economic rebalancing by China would be good for everyone, Chinese leaders have given little indication that they are moving decisively in this direction. With China's ever-increasing exports threatening to decimate European manufacturing, the EU has little choice but to embrace tariffs.

item.title: The Gospel of the Great Leader
item.description: North Korea’s communist regime has long functioned as a faith, repurposing Christian doctrine and imagery to deify its founder, Kim Il-sung, and his descendants. A new book traces how those religious influences transformed the Kim dynasty’s personality cult into a system that has endured across three generations.

item.title: Technology Is Not Above the Law
item.description: In arguing for a regulatory regime that is skewed entirely toward freeing developers to build online services, rather than placing any social obligations on them, the AI industry is using a playbook that Silicon Valley wrote 30 years ago. This time, however, the public seems less inclined to buy the industry's argument.

item.title: Superintelligent Democracy
item.description: Rather than framing the pursuit of AI capabilities as a race, we should turn the process into a democratic mission, with milestones set by the people, rather than on their behalf. Taiwan's own demonstration of mission-led governance, along with insights from the open-web community, show what is possible.

item.title: How Europe Can Save a Trillion Euros and Win the AI Race
item.description: If the risk Europe faces is losing access to frontier AI models, the solution is not necessarily to chase the labs that created them in the hopes of eventually pulling ahead. Instead, it is to build the capacity to make surviving that loss possible, such as by investing in AI infrastructure and training capabilities.

item.title: MDBs Are Becoming a New Global Safe Asset
item.description: Even as multilateralism faces an existential threat, multilateral development banks are not only surviving but thriving. Thanks to MDBs’ ability to borrow at costs close to that of the US Treasury, they have created a new class of de facto risk-free assets that could help underpin the global financial system.

item.title: Why US Bond Markets Are Trembling
item.description: What is the apparent fragility in the US bond market telling us? Since markets tend to be less wrong than those who comment on them regularly, their signals must be taken seriously, especially when they coincide with a relative softening in US inflation figures and other high-frequency economic indicators.

item.title: Look East for Lessons in Democratic Resistance
item.description: Pro-democracy activists often turn to Eastern and Central Europe for inspiration, while Asia’s remarkable democratic breakthroughs receive far less attention. Yet the continent’s recent struggles offer valuable lessons for those seeking to resist the global advance of authoritarianism.

item.title: Three Ways AI Will Change the Course of Humanity
item.description: The AI debate has largely focused on productivity gains and job displacement, but its consequences will reach much further By revolutionizing how we combat disease, wage wars, and stimulate income growth, AI could fundamentally alter the terms of human existence.

item.title: Global Economic Convergence Is Stalling
item.description: For a while, the world’s advanced economies (other than the US) were rapidly losing ground to their emerging counterparts. But the BRICS' catch-up momentum has stalled since 2016, not because the G7 has been doing better, but because everyone has been doing worse.

item.title: When a Big Energy Project Turns Bad
item.description: After hundreds of millions of dollars were invested by developing-country governments, and before a single watt of energy was transferred, the CASA-1000 infrastructure project in Central Asia has effectively failed. The international institutions that conceived, financed, and promoted the project must answer for this.
